note: THE SELF-LOOP IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE MEASURE IS NOT COGRAPH'S EXISTING markov. Definition, eqs(9) p1485, (11) p1486 and (20) p1489 with the W construction p1494: set a_ii=1 for every i, W=A/rowSums(A), c=the left eigenvector of W at eigenvalue1 normalised to sum1, Z=(I-W+1c')^-1, M=(I-Z+E Zdg)diag(1/c), and c_IEC(j)=(n-1)/sum_{i!=j} m_ij. M is the Kemeny-Snell mean first passage matrix in the convention m_ij=E[steps from i until j is first reached], so eq(20) sums DOWN column j and the score is a reciprocal mean first passage time INTO j. Page1494 states the construction twice, in the body and in the Table1 note: 'the diagonal entries of its adjacency matrix A=[a_ij] were set to one and its influence network was computed as W=[w_ij]=a_ij/sum_j^n a_ij', following French1956. Footnote10 p1484 gives the reason - 'Given w_ii>0 for any i, all strong networks must be regular', regular meaning aperiodic - and footnote9 p1483 the periodic counterexample. THE LEDGER'S LONG-STANDING ASSUMPTION THAT markov IS IEC UP TO AN N VERSUS N-1 NUMERATOR IS WRONG: markov ALSO omits the self-loop, and that difference is not a rescaling. Computed this session, the largest within-graph spread of iec/markov over the 21 connected five-node graphs is 0.096, and the two rank the nodes differently on 2 of those 21; on the Krackhardt kite iec is 0.069051322 0.069051322 0.052899126 0.103448276 0.052899126 0.099984987 0.099984987 0.055384615 0.018730489 0.010291595 against markov's 0.102457598 0.102457598 0.077345179 0.158102767 0.077345179 0.149691514 0.149691514 0.077669903 0.025856496 0.014270425. markov IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNCHANGED; iec ships as a separate measure. REDUCIBLE INPUT IS REFUSED, NOT EXTENDED, AND THIS DEPARTS FROM THE BATCH47 PRECEDENT ON PURPOSE: for a reducible W the eigenvalue-one eigenspace has one dimension per closed class so c is undetermined and diag(1/c) undefined, and worse, eq(11) DOES NOT ANNOUNCE THE FAILURE - with Z block diagonal a cross-class pair has z_ij=0 and eq(11) returns the entirely finite m_ij=z_jj/c_j where the true mean first passage time is infinite. Batch47 could apply a reachability mask because ITS source states a zero rule for an unreachable pair; this source states none, and a component-wise reading would additionally have to invent whether the n-1 of eq(20) counts the component or the network. cograph therefore tests irreducibility by boolean closure BEFORE any solve and returns NA at every node with a cograph_undefined_measure warning - never a silent zero and never a finite wrong number. n=1 is NA too, eq(20) dividing by n-1=0; an empty graph returns no scores. An isolate never scores on its own because a graph containing one is reducible. DIRECTION IS KEPT because W is a matrix of directed influence, row i being what actor i attends to, and the measure then needs a STRONGLY connected digraph; there is no in/out/all variant so mode, cutoff and invert_weights are ignored. WEIGHTS ARE DROPPED DELIBERATELY: a_ii=1 is calibrated against a_ij=1, so rescaling the weights would silently re-weight each actor's self-reliance against the network, and the source demonstrates only the binary case. Loops in the input are absorbed by the mandated unit diagonal and parallel edges collapse. normalized=True max-scales, the source stating no normalization. Marked COSTLY: one boolean closure and two dense n x n solves. Zoo2.180 (p104) transcribes the source faithfully, renaming c to v; the sibling labels TEC (eq18) and MEC (eqs21-23) of the same paper are NOT covered. No author or third-party code exists

note: THE DENOMINATOR OF THE TRIANGLE SHARE IS TNTS, NOT THE NUMBER OF TRIANGLES, AND THE PAPER SETTLES IT RATHER THAN THE ZOO: eq(1) p3 is C(v)=sum over u with 1<=dist(u,v)<=d of k_u(1+TP(u))/dist(u,v)^2 with TP(u)=NTS(u)/TNTS, and eq(2) p4 is Lhc(v)=sum over w in the OPEN neighbourhood tau(v) of C(w). Immediately after defining TNTS=sum_u NTS(u) the source writes that 'the total number of triangle structure exists in the network are 1/3 * TNTS', so TNTS=3*Delta and sum_u TP(u)=1 exactly. Zoo 2.221 (comparison-matrix label 'Lhc method', encyclopedia heading 'Lhc index') transcribes the structure of both equations correctly but names the denominator 'Delta, the total number of triangular structures in the network', which read literally is three times too small; on the Krackhardt kite the paper's reading scores node1 at 3305/33=100.15152 where the Zoo's literal wording gives 1380/11=125.45455 (Kendall tau1.0 on that particular graph, but the two are not related by a monotone transform in general). cograph follows the paper; the divergence is reproduced in kite_worked.csv only to show its size. THE COEFFICIENT WAS READ OFF THE PAGE IMAGE AT 400dpi, NOT FROM pdftotext, which mangles the stacked fraction into '13 * TNTS'; a transcription error there would move every score by up to 25 percent. BOTH NEIGHBOURHOODS ARE OPEN: Phi(v) is 1<=dist<=lhc_radius, the focal node excluded because dist^2(vv)=0 would divide by zero and unreachable nodes falling outside the radius so no infinity arises; tau(v) is N(v). It follows, though the source does not remark on it, that v DOES enter its own Lhc(v), lying at distance1 inside Phi(w) for every neighbour w. TRIANGLE-FREE GRAPHS ARE AN EXPLICIT COGRAPH DECISION THE SOURCE NEVER MAKES: every tree, star, path, even cycle and bipartite graph has TNTS=0 and TP(u)=0/0 at every node. Because TNTS is a sum of nonnegative counts it vanishes exactly when every numerator NTS(u) vanishes too, so there is no share to distribute and no node with a claim on one; TP is written as ZERO and the index reduces to the pure sum over w in N(v) of sum over u in Phi(w) of k_u/dist(uw)^2, the neighbour-and-location half of the hybrid with the triangle half contributing nothing. The test is made on TNTS BEFORE ANY DIVISION so no 0/0 is evaluated; this is a documented branch, not a silent zero, and NA or an error would refuse every tree. RAW SCORES ARE NOT COMPONENT-LOCAL because TNTS is a global sum: attaching a disconnected component carrying a triangle rescales every TP and moves every score (the kite plus a disjoint triangle moves all ten scores), while attaching a TRIANGLE-FREE component - an isolate or a disjoint edge - changes nothing, since it changes no degree, no triangle and no finite distance. Both halves are asserted. ISOLATES score a DERIVED zero because tau(v) is empty and eq(2) is an empty sum; a singleton and every node of an edgeless graph score zero for the same reason; empty graphs return no scores. lhc_radius IS THE SOURCE'S OWN PARAMETER d, EXPOSED WITH THE SOURCE'S DEFAULT 2 (p4, 'the distance ranged d is set to be 2'), which section3 sweeps over eleven real networks reporting 'the optimal value of d is about 2-3' and stability beyond 3 (p7). At lhc_radius=1 the ball collapses to the neighbours and C(v) becomes sum over u in N(v) of k_u(1+TP(u)); at or above the graph radius the ball has saturated and the score stops moving. Domain is a whole number >=1; zero, negative, fractional, NA, Inf, non-scalar and non-numeric raise cograph_bad_parameter rather than being truncated. Simple undirected unweighted skeleton; direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are dropped because k_u is a count, dist(uv) a hop count and NTS(u) combinatorial; mode, cutoff and invert_weights ignored; normalized=True max-scales, the source stating no normalization. NOT marked costly: one all-pairs shortest-path solve and one A.A product, the same order as closeness or gravity, neither of which is held back from type='all'. A directed, weighted or multigraph input is symmetrised, its weights and parallel lines collapsed and its loops dropped, SILENTLY, which is the convention every other undirected-domain measure in centrality() already follows; warning on each would be noisy and inconsistent with its twenty-odd siblings, and the projection is documented on the help page and asserted in the tests. No in/out/all reading exists, so the measure is in the no-mode family and cutoff and invert_weights are ignored. NOT MARKED COSTLY: the source claims O(n<k>^2) 'Local information' in Table4 p218 and the kernel is one masked matrix product plus elementwise work, so it stays in type='all'. THE ISOLATED K2 IS THE ONE 0/0 AND IT IS RESOLVED, NOT REFUSED, WHICH IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM BATCH49: k_i+k_j-2 vanishes only when both endpoints have degree one, since every endpoint of a line has degree at least one, and there p=0 and U=(1-0-1)(1-0-1)=0 as well, so the importance being split is EXACTLY ZERO while the split of it is 0/0. Because W is a SHARE of I and the two shares sum to one wherever defined, every admissible split of an exactly zero importance gives an exactly zero contribution - the answer does not depend on resolving the indeterminacy - so the share is written as zero WITH THE TEST TAKEN BEFORE THE DIVISION and both K2 nodes score 1. THE SOURCE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THIS CASE (grepped for denominator/zero/undefined); the choice is cograph's and it follows the batch48 lhc precedent, where TNTS=0 makes TP a 0/0 on every triangle-free graph and is likewise written as zero because the denominator vanishes exactly where every numerator does. It deliberately does NOT follow batch49 iec, which returns NA on reducible input: there the closed form returns a FINITE WRONG NUMBER where the truth is infinite, so a value would be wrong; here every candidate value is the same value. Isolates, singletons, edgeless and disconnected input need no rule - an isolate has an empty sum and scores 0, and raw scores are component-local because nothing reaches past a node's second neighbours. normalized=True max-scales, the source stating no normalization. U>=0 always, since p<=k_i-1, so no score falls below its node's degree. note: THE ZOO CITES THE WRONG PAPER FOR THIS MEASURE. Zoo2.381 reference[350] is Sheng et al2020 PhysicaA541:123262 doi10.1016/j.physa.2019.123262, which defines the 'global and local structure' index of Zoo2.149, a different object; the real source is Sheng, Zhu, Wang, Wang and Hou2020, 'Identifying Influential Nodes of Complex Networks Based on Trust-Value', Algorithms13(11):280, doi10.3390/a13110280, fully open access, read this session from 200dpi page images of pages5, 6, 7 and10. Correct the ledger reference regardless of implementation. Definition eqs(2), (4), (5), (6), (7) and Algorithm1, pp5-7. THE DECISIVE CONVENTION IS THE DOMAIN OF EQ(4), NOT AN ITERATION COUNT: Algorithm1 line4 reads 'for CONNECTED node v_u, v_v in V' and Table3's caption says a dash means no edge, so the similarity map holds only the lines plus the diagonal and a NON-ADJACENT PAIR CONTRIBUTES 0, not the0.1 that initialises the lines. That makes the diagonal the only inhomogeneous term, reaching a line exactly through the triangles it carries, and makes the recursion contract at C=1. Pinning non-adjacent pairs at0.1 explains 0 of Table3's7 printed similarities and swaps karate positions8 and9 in Table5; reading Algorithm1 literally as a fixed sweep count explains 0 of7 at 1, 2, 3, 5 and10 sweeps and 7 of7 only at the fixed point. THE MEASURE HAS NO VALUE ON A COMPONENT THAT HAS LINES BUT NO TRIANGLE, AND COGRAPH RETURNS NA THERE. With no triangle the recursion is homogeneous, its least nonnegative fixed point is s=0 on every line, and eq(2) is 0/0. That class is not a corner case - every path, tree, star, even cycle and complete bipartite graph is in it, and so is the Petersen graph - and 1,394 of the 5,532 retained fixtures fall in it. THE 1/d_j FALLBACK RECOMMENDED BY candidate_review48 WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: unlike the vanishing denominators of batch50 dil and batch48 lhc, this quotient is NOT determined by its numerator, since the ratios need only sum to one over N_j and nothing in the source chooses between the ways of doing that, so a different admissible choice gives a different score; adopting 1/d_j would silently turn the measure into a degree-ratio PageRank over the whole triangle-free class while still calling it Trust-PageRank. This FOLLOWS BATCH49 iec, which returns NA rather than the finite number its closed form would otherwise print, and deliberately does NOT follow batch50. A SECOND READING WAS ALSO REJECTED: starting the recursion at the source's0.1 rather than at zero would define the sub-class on which that start is itself a fixed point (K2, P3, stars, C4, complete bipartite graphs, spectral radius exactly1 with the uniform vector fixed), where it gives Rs=1/d_j independently of the constant's SIZE; rejected because the value is then an artifact of the initialisation being UNIFORM rather than of the graph, because it leaves P4 and longer, C5 and longer, trees and Petersen undefined anyway, and because separating a frozen start from an exponentially decaying zero needs a numerical threshold where cograph settles the question STRUCTURALLY by a boolean closure asking which lines can reach a triangle. The paper's own Table3 is reproduced only at the fixed point, so the initialisation is scaffolding, not a modelling choice. The NA covers the whole component because an undefined trust column makes eq(7) undefined for everything that solves against it, and the undefined set was checked over 5,417 fixtures to be EXACTLY the components having lines but no triangle. AN ISOLATE IS NOT IN THE CLASS: it is never a j in eq(2), and eq(7) gives it the bare (1-alpha)/n through an empty sum, so a graph with isolates has scores summing to less than one. THE DOMAIN DOES NOT MOVE WITH k, k=1 included: the similarity ratio is part of the trust-value at every mixing weight, and switching a measure's domain on the knife-edge value k=1 would also mean an == on a double. T IS COLUMN-STOCHASTIC (measured max |sum-1| 1.110223e-16) because both ratios are normalised over N_j and s is symmetric, so eq(7) is an ordinary damped PageRank with a unique fixed point and THE ITERATION COUNT IS A TOLERANCE, NOT A MODELLING CHOICE; tpr_tol and tpr_max_iter are exposed and a recursion still moving at the bound raises cograph_no_converge. BOTH CONVERGENCE TESTS ARE RELATIVE, NOT ABSOLUTE, AND THAT IS A FIX TO THE STOPPING RULE RATHER THAN A WIDENED TOLERANCE: the similarities on one graph span twenty orders of magnitude (2.36e-2 down to 2.75e-20 on fixture1224 at C=0.2), an absolute test at1e-14 stopped six sweeps early there and gave a 1.85e-5 scaled error against the direct solve, and with the relative test it agrees to 2.4e-16. verified_scope: directed or undirected graphs with nonnegative weights (unit weights when unweighted); lric_quota 0.5 and 0.7; lric_path_length Inf and 2; NA with a classed warning past enumeration_limit subset sums per node
note: c_ij = w_ij over the smallest critical group of j in which i is pivotal (quota = lric_quota times the incoming weight); c*_ij = best product over simple paths; LRIC(i) = sum_j c*_ij u_j with u_j the share of all outgoing weight. DEFAULT PATH LENGTH IS UNLIMITED, following the definition ("all simple paths"); the printed tables need at least 4 arcs, and the authors' program defaults to 3, which gives 0.076 and 0.567 at nodes 6 and 8 where Table15 prints 0.078 and 0.598. The max-product closure equals simple-path enumeration because no direct influence exceeds 1. A group meeting the quota exactly is critical; comparisons carry a relative slack of 1e-12. The Zoo's plain row sum is NOT what the working paper aggregates. Scores are not rescaled to sum to one (slric does that). The sibling label LRIC (PPR) remains blocked: no paper equation read.

note: TC(v) = mean over ordered pairs of the exp(-beta hops)-weighted share of simple paths through v, divisor (N-1)(N-2). Path cost is the hop count, as in the worked example. A pair without a path adds 0 with the divisor unchanged, the convention of the authors' program (the paper is silent). The program divides by (N-1) on directed graphs, contradicting eq(8); eq(8) is followed. NO SINGLE DEFAULT IN THE SOURCE: beta is 2.0 in the example, the experiments concentrate on 0.1, the author GUI pre-fills 1; cograph defaults to 0.1.
